guide: Use Claude Code to sort the files on your laptop and in Google Drive into a review folder, without deleting anything. You need Claude Code installed, a terminal, and access to the folders you want tidied.
1. Install Claude Code from Anthropic and open a terminal in the folder you want to tidy.
1. Ask Claude to scan the folder and list what is there: file types, sizes, duplicates and old files.
1. Tell Claude your rules for what counts as clutter, such as duplicates, installers, old downloads and empty folders.
1. Have Claude create a folder called "To Be Deleted" inside the folder you are tidying.
1. Ask Claude to move the files that match your rules into that folder, and never to delete anything.
1. Repeat on each laptop folder and hard drive, then on Google Drive, either through the Drive desktop app's synced folder or by moving files into a review folder in Drive itself.
1. Open "To Be Deleted", check what is in it, and move back anything you want to keep.
1. When you are happy, delete the folder yourself.
Watch out: Claude only moves files and never deletes. You do the deleting, and only after you have looked through the folder.

```
You are helping me tidy my files safely. Work in <folder path> on my <Windows/Mac/Linux> computer. I use <Google Drive for desktop / no cloud storage>.
Step 1: scan the folder and report file types, total sizes, duplicates and files not opened since <date or "a year ago">. Do not change anything yet.
Step 2: propose a list of rules for what counts as clutter, using these as a start: <duplicates, installers, old downloads, empty folders>. Wait for my approval of the rules.
Step 3: create a folder called "To Be Deleted" inside <folder path>. Move every file that matches the approved rules into it, keeping the original sub-folder structure so I can put things back.
Hard rules: never delete, overwrite or rename any file. Never touch files outside <folder path>. If two files would clash, stop and ask me.
Finish by returning a log of everything you moved (original path, new path, reason) and the total space the folder now holds, so I can review it and delete it myself.
```
